about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1014-181424-b6f9) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all six model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, under a minute); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out years; only Lucidity scored them. Data is from FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): the target rate from the Federal Reserve Board, Treasury yields from the Treasury, unemployment and CPI from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
title: Fed rate hikes

card.ask: Will the Fed raise rates next month? From yields, inflation and unemployment.
card.why: Ordinary logistic regression on all 8 columns, no tuning. It's the best answer here without agents.

blurb: A model predicts whether the Fed raises its target rate next month, from Treasury yields, inflation and unemployment known at the end of this month, 1985-2026. The repo scores 0.462 log loss and plain regression on all 8 columns scores 0.342, so the goal is 0.3409. Six kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on 2005-2014. Lucidity scores every attempt on 2015-2026, years the agents never see, and recommends the best.
split: Trained on 1985-2004, tuned on 2005-2014, tested on 2015-2026. Agents never see the test years; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Coin flip (always 50%)
references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

references.label: Always guess the usual hike rate
references.why: Say the same chance of a hike every month: how often it happened in training.

references.label: Plain logistic regression, all 8 columns
references.why: Ordinary logistic regression on every column, no tuning. The five-minute model.

about_repo: bundled Fed-hike model: monthly 1985-2026, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: fedkit: hiked this month + 10-year yield, logistic regression, Fed months 1985-2026, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.3409 or lower (plain logistic regression on all 8 columns scores 0.3416; the repo scores 0.462) for predicting whether the Fed raises its target rate next month, without AUC dropping. Tune on the dev split. The no-lookahead tests must keep passing. Ask the owner which model families to try (kNN, SVM, lasso or ridge logistic regression, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Compare the requested model families on the dev split, select the strongest candidate without compromising AUC or the no-lookahead guarantees, then integrate and verify the winner against the held-out log-loss target. Owner input is needed to choose which model-family experiments to run.

nodes.title: Experiment with selected model families and compare on dev
nodes.prompt: For the model family selected by the owner, implement it behind the existing model interface and tune its hyperparameters using only the dev split (2005–2014). Preserve chronological split behavior and no-lookahead feature semantics. Report dev log loss and AUC, and keep the experiment independently selectable so its result can be compared with other selected families.
strategies: kNN. Implement a leakage-safe, scaled kNN classifier; tune neighbors and weighting on dev.
SVM. Implement scaled SVM classification with dev-tuned kernel and regularization; use probability calibration suitable for log loss.
Lasso logistic regression. Implement scaled L1-regularized logistic regression and tune its regularization on dev.
Ridge logistic regression. Implement scaled L2-regularized logistic regression and tune its regularization on dev.
Random forest. Implement a random forest and tune complexity and class/probability handling on dev.
Boosted trees. Implement gradient-boosted trees and tune depth, shrinkage, and regularization on dev.

nodes.title: Select and integrate best dev candidate
nodes.prompt: After the family experiments finish, compare their dev log loss and AUC, choose the candidate with lowest dev log loss subject to no AUC regression, and make it the default model. Run the held-out evaluation and no-lookahead tests; do not tune on held-out results.

questions.question: Which model families should agents try in parallel? Select one or more; the recommended choice is to try all six.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Scaled neighborhood methods may capture local patterns, but the dataset is small.
options.approach: Implement a leakage-safe, scaled kNN classifier; tune neighbors and weighting on dev.

options.label: SVM
options.note: A scaled nonlinear SVM can model interactions with calibrated probabilities.
options.approach: Implement scaled SVM classification with dev-tuned kernel and regularization; use probability calibration suitable for log loss.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Sparse regularization can control overfitting among correlated indicators.
options.approach: Implement scaled L1-regularized logistic regression and tune its regularization on dev.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: A stable regularized linear baseline suits this small time-series dataset.
options.approach: Implement scaled L2-regularized logistic regression and tune its regularization on dev.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Trees can find threshold effects, though the limited event count may constrain them.
options.approach: Implement a random forest and tune complexity and class/probability handling on dev.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Boosted trees may learn useful nonlinear interactions in the rate-cycle features.
options.approach: Implement gradient-boosted trees and tune depth, shrinkage, and regularization on dev.
